summary: You can set requests and limits for the web, task, EE control plane and Redis containers (web/task/ee/redis_resource_requirements, each defaulting to requests of 100m CPU and 128Mi). Setting both gives a higher Quality of Service class so control pods are less likely to be evicted, and task container limits determine control capacity, with each job costing one unit.
questions: What are the default resource requests for automation controller containers?
Why set both requests and limits for controller pods?
How do task container limits affect controller capacity?

answer_card.title: Controller container resource settings
answer_card.answer_md:
| Field | Container | Default requests |
|---|---|---|
| `web_resource_requirements` | Web | CPU 100m, memory 128Mi |
| `task_resource_requirements` | Task | CPU 100m, memory 128Mi |
| `ee_resource_requirements` | EE control plane | CPU 100m, memory 128Mi |
| `redis_resource_requirements` | Redis | CPU 100m, memory 128Mi |

Setting both requests and limits gives the pods a higher Quality of Service class, so they are less likely to be evicted. The task container's limits set control capacity; controlling a job costs 1 unit.
